authoritativeScope.lessonBlockMeaning: Each lesson is a teachable topic block, typically 1-3 class periods depending on diagnostic evidence.

criteria.Evidence: Strong cumulative mastery across all prerequisite strands; approximately 85%+ on the common readiness benchmark; no critical strand below about 75%; strong independence and representation/justification performance.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Place in Grade 10 AP Precalculus. Assign a short summer bridge only for isolated weak strands.

criteria.Evidence: Core skills mostly secure but one or more Algebra 2/trig/function strands remain inconsistent; strong growth trajectory.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Place in the readiness section with eligibility for Transfer Gate 1 after the first major Grade 10 unit.

criteria.Evidence: Several prerequisite strands are not yet durable or independent.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Remain in the readiness section through Grade 10; course is designed so successful completion leads directly to Grade 11 AP Precalculus.

common.title: Grade 9 Mathematics - AP Precalculus Readiness
common.destination: Evidence-based placement into Grade 10 AP Precalculus or the Grade 10 AP-Readiness pathway.

units.title: Diagnostic & Algebra Bridge
units.intent: Identify prerequisite gaps quickly, then address only what is necessary so all students can access a rigorous common course.
units.coreFocus: Entry diagnostic; number fluency; fractions/decimals/percent; signed numbers; order of operations; exponent rules; equation basics.
units.apReadinessPurpose: Build a common baseline without lowering the ceiling; create individual targeted-review and extension plans.

lessons.title: Entry Diagnostic & Mathematical Profile
subtopics: Mixed diagnostic across arithmetic, algebra, functions, graph reading, and prior geometry; error analysis; calculator/non-calculator habits.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate current prerequisite knowledge; classify errors as conceptual, procedural, or attention-based; set 2-3 personal mastery targets.

lessons.title: Number and Expression Fluency
subtopics: Signed numbers; fractions/decimals/percent; order of operations; distributive property; combining like terms.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions accurately; move fluently among fraction, decimal, and percent forms; simplify expressions using structure.

lessons.title: Exponent Rules & Equation Solving
subtopics: Integer exponents; zero/negative exponents; one- and two-step equations; checking solutions.
learningOutcomes: Apply core exponent laws; solve foundational equations; verify solutions by substitution and explain invalid steps.

units.title: Linear Relationships, Equations & Inequalities
units.intent: Develop complete linear-function and equation fluency in analytical, graphical, numerical, and contextual forms.
units.coreFocus: Expressions; multi-step equations; literal equations; slope; linear forms; graph/table/equation connections; linear inequalities; modeling.
units.apReadinessPurpose: AP prerequisite: linear functions, algebraic manipulation, equations/inequalities, multiple representations.

lessons.title: Algebraic Expressions & Multi-Step Equations
subtopics: Distributive property; collecting terms; variables on both sides; identities/contradictions; proportional equations.
learningOutcomes: Simplify expressions; solve multi-step linear equations; classify one/no/infinitely-many-solution cases and justify the result.

lessons.title: Literal Equations & Formula Rearrangement
subtopics: Solve formulas for a variable; units; dimensional reasonableness; substitution.
learningOutcomes: Rearrange formulas algebraically; substitute with units; interpret the meaning of a solved-for quantity.

lessons.title: Slope and Rate of Change
subtopics: Slope from points/table/graph; positive/negative/zero/undefined slope; unit rate; average rate of change.
learningOutcomes: Calculate and interpret slope; connect slope to constant rate of change; distinguish input and output units.

lessons.title: Representations of Linear Functions
subtopics: Slope-intercept, point-slope, standard form; intercepts; graphing; tables; writing equations.
learningOutcomes: Move among linear representations; construct an equation from data or conditions; identify intercepts and explain their contextual meaning.

lessons.title: Linear Inequalities
subtopics: One-variable inequalities; compound inequalities; interval notation; graphing on a number line.
learningOutcomes: Solve and represent linear/compound inequalities; reverse inequality signs correctly when required; express solution sets in interval notation.

lessons.title: Linear Modeling & Residual Thinking
subtopics: Scatterplots; informal line of fit; linear regression with technology; residual idea; model limitations.
learningOutcomes: Build and interpret a linear model; use residuals informally to judge fit; state assumptions and limitations of a model.

units.title: Systems, Absolute Value & Piecewise Models
units.intent: Use systems and piecewise structures to model situations with multiple constraints or changing rules.
units.coreFocus: Systems by graph/substitution/elimination; 3-variable systems; systems of inequalities; absolute-value equations/inequalities; piecewise functions.
units.apReadinessPurpose: AP prerequisite: systems in 2/3 variables; familiarity with piecewise functions.

lessons.title: Systems by Graphing and Substitution
subtopics: Intersection meaning; graphing systems; substitution; consistency/dependence.
learningOutcomes: Solve systems graphically and algebraically; connect a solution to an intersection; classify consistent/inconsistent/dependent systems.

lessons.title: Systems by Elimination
subtopics: Linear combinations; strategic multiplication; exact solutions; checking.
learningOutcomes: Solve 2x2 systems efficiently using elimination; select a method based on structure; verify ordered-pair solutions.

lessons.title: Systems in Three Variables
subtopics: Elimination in 3x3 systems; organized work; contextual systems.
learningOutcomes: Solve accessible 3-variable systems; organize elimination logically; interpret the resulting triple in context.

lessons.title: Systems of Inequalities
subtopics: Half-planes; boundary lines; feasible region; constraint interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Represent simultaneous inequality constraints graphically and contextually.
lessons.requiredGrade9Coverage: Graph 2-variable systems of linear inequalities and identify/test feasible regions.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred beyond this course: formal linear-programming optimization algorithms.

lessons.title: Absolute Value Equations & Inequalities
subtopics: Distance interpretation; two-case equations; compound inequalities; graphical interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Connect absolute value to distance and solve standard equations/inequalities.
lessons.requiredGrade9Coverage: Solve standard absolute-value equations/inequalities using distance and case reasoning.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not developed within this course: a full transformed absolute-value function unit or parameter analysis.

lessons.title: Piecewise-Defined Functions
subtopics: Reading/writing simple piecewise rules; evaluating at breakpoints; endpoint inclusion; context models.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate and graph simple piecewise functions and communicate domain conditions precisely.
lessons.requiredGrade9Coverage: Read, evaluate, and graph 2-3 piece functions, mainly linear/simple quadratic pieces; construct a simple rule from context.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: AP-style rates across intervals, continuity-style analysis, complex nested pieces, and advanced modeling for later.

units.title: Function Language & Multiple Representations
units.intent: Make function thinking the organizing language of the course and prepare students to reason across representations.
units.coreFocus: Function notation; domain/range; interval notation; average rate of change; transformations; composition/inverse concepts; interpretation in context.
units.apReadinessPurpose: Creates the function fluency needed for every AP Precalculus unit.

lessons.title: Relations, Functions & Function Notation
subtopics: Input/output; vertical line test; f(x); independent/dependent variables; discrete vs continuous.
learningOutcomes: Use function notation and distinguish functions from nonfunctions across common representations.
lessons.requiredGrade9Coverage: Determine function status; evaluate notation; identify meaningful input/output quantities and domains.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not included within this course: advanced implicit-function or parametric-function treatment.

lessons.title: Domain, Range & Interval Notation
subtopics: Domain/range from graphs, tables, formulas, contexts; restrictions; set/interval notation.
learningOutcomes: Determine domain and range from multiple representations; apply meaningful contextual restrictions; express intervals precisely.

lessons.title: Increasing, Decreasing, Extrema & Intercepts
subtopics: Intervals of increase/decrease; zeros; y-intercepts; relative extrema; sign of a function.
learningOutcomes: Describe key graph characteristics using interval language; connect zeros to equations; interpret extrema and intercepts in context.

lessons.title: Transformations of Parent Functions
subtopics: Translations; reflections; vertical/horizontal scaling; order of transformations.
learningOutcomes: Predict and construct transformed graphs; write transformed equations; explain how parameters affect graph features.

lessons.title: Average Rate of Change
subtopics: Difference quotient over an interval; secant slope; units; comparison across intervals.
learningOutcomes: Compute average rate of change; interpret it contextually; compare changing behavior across intervals and representations.

lessons.title: Composition and Inverse Concepts
subtopics: Composition as process chaining; input restrictions; one-to-one idea; inverse as reversing a process.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate simple compositions; interpret composition in context; determine when an inverse relationship is reasonable and verify by reversal.

units.title: Quadratic Functions & Equations
units.intent: Achieve full quadratic mastery so students can enter polynomial modeling without procedural gaps.
units.coreFocus: Standard/factored/vertex forms; factoring; completing square; quadratic formula; discriminant; complex solutions; inequalities; modeling.
units.apReadinessPurpose: AP prerequisite: full quadratic proficiency; prepares polynomial work.

lessons.title: Quadratic Patterns & Graph Features
subtopics: Second differences; parabola; vertex; axis of symmetry; intercepts; opening direction.
learningOutcomes: Recognize quadratic behavior from tables/graphs; identify key graph features; connect second differences to quadratic change.

lessons.title: Three Forms of a Quadratic
subtopics: Standard, factored, vertex forms; information revealed by each form; converting when efficient.
learningOutcomes: Interpret coefficients/parameters in each form; choose the most useful form for a task; convert among forms strategically.

lessons.title: Factoring Quadratics
subtopics: GCF; trinomial factoring; difference of squares; zero-product property.
learningOutcomes: Factor quadratic expressions completely; solve equations using factoring; connect factors, zeros, and x-intercepts.

lessons.title: Completing the Square
subtopics: Perfect-square trinomials; deriving vertex form; solving equations.
learningOutcomes: Complete the square accurately; use it to rewrite quadratics in vertex form; solve quadratic equations by square-root methods.

lessons.title: Quadratic Formula, Discriminant & Complex Numbers
subtopics: Quadratic formula; discriminant; i; complex conjugates; exact vs approximate roots.
learningOutcomes: Solve any quadratic equation; predict number/type of roots from the discriminant; express nonreal solutions using complex numbers.

lessons.title: Quadratic Inequalities
subtopics: Sign intervals; graph-based solution; test intervals; compound solution sets.
learningOutcomes: Solve quadratic inequalities algebraically and graphically; use zeros to partition the number line; express final sets in interval notation.

lessons.title: Quadratic Modeling & Optimization
subtopics: Projectile/area/revenue-style models; vertex interpretation; regression; model limitations.
learningOutcomes: Construct or fit quadratic models; use the vertex to optimize a contextual quantity; state reasonable domain and limitations.

units.title: Polynomial Functions & Algebra
units.intent: Build the algebraic structure and graph reasoning that directly precede AP Precalculus Unit 1.
units.coreFocus: Polynomial operations; factoring; zeros/multiplicity; factor/remainder theorems; division; end behavior; graphs from structure.
units.apReadinessPurpose: Direct bridge into AP Precalculus Unit 1.

lessons.title: Polynomial Operations
subtopics: Degree; leading coefficient; addition/subtraction/multiplication; special products.
learningOutcomes: Perform polynomial operations accurately; identify degree/leading term; use structure to simplify calculations.

lessons.title: Factoring Beyond Quadratics
subtopics: Grouping; sum/difference of cubes; repeated factors; substitution patterns.
learningOutcomes: Factor a range of polynomial expressions; select a productive factoring strategy; verify by multiplication.

lessons.title: Zeros, Factors & Multiplicity
subtopics: Factor-zero connection; multiplicity; graph crossing/touching; real vs complex zeros.
learningOutcomes: Connect zeros, factors, and intercepts; infer graph behavior from multiplicity; represent a polynomial from given zeros.

lessons.title: Polynomial Division & Theorems
subtopics: Long division; synthetic division; remainder theorem; factor theorem.
learningOutcomes: Divide polynomials; evaluate efficiently with the remainder theorem; determine whether a binomial is a factor.

lessons.title: Polynomial Graphs & End Behavior
subtopics: Leading-term test; odd/even degree; end behavior; turning points as qualitative feature.
learningOutcomes: Predict end behavior; sketch a reasonable graph from structure; connect algebraic form to global and local graph features.

units.title: Rational & Radical Foundations
units.intent: Provide the rational-expression and radical fluency needed to avoid algebra becoming the barrier in AP Precalculus.
units.coreFocus: Rational expressions/restrictions; rational equations; radicals; rational exponents; radical equations; extraneous solutions.
units.apReadinessPurpose: Supports rational-function and exponential/logarithmic work in AP Precalculus.

lessons.title: Rational Expressions & Restrictions
subtopics: Factoring; simplifying; excluded values; multiplication/division; common denominators.
learningOutcomes: Simplify rational expressions while preserving restrictions; perform operations; distinguish equivalent expressions from equivalent functions with domain restrictions.

lessons.title: Rational Equations
subtopics: LCD strategy; extraneous/undefined values; proportions; contextual rates.
learningOutcomes: Solve rational equations; reject invalid values; explain how domain restrictions affect the solution set.

lessons.title: Radicals & Rational Exponents
subtopics: Nth roots; rational exponents; exponent laws; simplifying radicals; operations.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite between radical and rational-exponent forms; simplify radical expressions; apply exponent rules consistently.

lessons.title: Radical Equations
subtopics: Isolating radicals; powers; checking; extraneous solutions.
learningOutcomes: Solve radical equations; identify why extraneous solutions arise; verify solutions in the original equation.

units.title: Exponential Functions & Sequences
units.intent: Develop the multiplicative-change thinking that will become AP Precalculus Unit 2.
units.coreFocus: Exponent laws; arithmetic/geometric sequences; exponential growth/decay; compare linear/quadratic/exponential change.
units.apReadinessPurpose: AP prerequisite: exponent rules and exponential familiarity; preview of AP Unit 2.

lessons.title: Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
subtopics: Recursive/explicit forms; common difference/ratio; discrete domain.
learningOutcomes: Identify arithmetic vs geometric change; write explicit/recursive rules; interpret parameters and domain.

lessons.title: Exponential Functions
subtopics: Growth/decay factors; initial value; graphs; domain/range; asymptotic behavior.
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret exponential functions; identify initial value and growth factor; compare exponential graphs.

lessons.title: Equivalent Exponential Forms
subtopics: Exponent laws; percent rate vs growth factor; equivalent bases; rational exponents.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite exponential expressions usefully; convert between percent rate and factor; explain how equivalent forms reveal different information.

lessons.title: Growth/Decay Modeling & Family Comparison
subtopics: Compound growth; decay; data fitting; compare linear, quadratic, exponential patterns.
learningOutcomes: Select an appropriate model family from data/context; fit and interpret an exponential model; justify model choice using rate patterns/residual evidence.

units.title: Right-Triangle Trigonometry & Coordinate Applications
units.intent: Secure the trigonometric prerequisite for AP Precalculus while keeping geometry limited to what supports function work.
units.coreFocus: Pythagorean theorem; similarity connections; sine/cosine/tangent; inverse trig; angles of elevation/depression; distance/slope applications.
units.apReadinessPurpose: AP prerequisite: right-triangle trigonometry; prepares AP Unit 3.

lessons.title: Right Triangles, Similarity & Pythagorean Relationships
subtopics: Pythagorean theorem; similarity; side ratios; coordinate distance.
learningOutcomes: Solve missing-side problems; use similarity to justify constant trig ratios; connect distance formula to right-triangle structure.

lessons.title: Sine, Cosine & Tangent Ratios
subtopics: SOH-CAH-TOA; reference angle in right triangle; exact vs approximate values; calculator use.
learningOutcomes: Choose and use an appropriate trig ratio; solve for missing sides; interpret ratios as relationships, not memorized labels only.

lessons.title: Inverse Trigonometry
subtopics: arcsin/arccos/arctan; solve for angles; reasonableness; calculator mode.
learningOutcomes: Determine unknown angles using inverse trig; check reasonableness; communicate angle units and precision.

lessons.title: Applied Trigonometry
subtopics: Angles of elevation/depression; indirect measurement; coordinate slope/angle connections.
learningOutcomes: Model and solve contextual right-triangle problems; draw a valid diagram; state assumptions and units.

units.title: AP Readiness Integration & Placement
units.intent: Synthesize prerequisite strands, test independence, and place students into the Grade 10 pathway using evidence rather than a single score.
units.coreFocus: Transformations/composition/inverses revisit; regression/model choice; mixed representations; AP-style reasoning; cumulative readiness capstone.
units.apReadinessPurpose: Determines Grade 10 pathway while closing remaining prerequisite gaps.

lessons.title: Function Toolkit Synthesis
subtopics: Domain/range; transformations; composition; inverse; rates of change; piecewise review.
learningOutcomes: Use multiple function tools in one task; choose a representation strategically; explain reasoning with precise notation.

lessons.title: Model Selection Across Families
subtopics: Linear/quadratic/exponential models; regression; residuals; assumptions; extrapolation cautions.
learningOutcomes: Select and justify a model; interpret parameters; use residual/context evidence; identify unsafe extrapolation.

lessons.title: AP-Style Multiple Representations
subtopics: Graph-table-formula-context translation; non-calculator algebra; calculator-supported analysis; written rationale.
learningOutcomes: Translate among representations; sustain multi-step reasoning; provide a concise rationale for conclusions.

lessons.title: Cumulative AP Readiness Capstone
subtopics: Mixed prerequisite assessment; error correction; student reflection; summer/Grade 10 transition plan.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate mastery across all prerequisite strands; correct and explain errors; identify the appropriate next pathway and targeted summer actions.
